chunks: From him, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Usaym al-Nakhas, from Muawiya ibn Ammar, who said:

I heard Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) saying: 'Indeed, a man from among you lives in the neighborhood, so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, will use him as an argument against his neighbors on the Day of Resurrection. It will be said to them: 'Was not so-and-so among you? Did you not hear his speech? Did you not hear his weeping at night?' So he will be the argument of Allah against them.'

key_terms.بُكَاءَهُ فِي اللَّيْلِ: His weeping at night (referring to night prayers/devotion)

ai.seo_question: How does a righteous person serve as an argument against their neighbors on the Day of Judgment?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from Al-Kafi underscores the communal responsibility of *al-amr bi-l-ma'ruf wa-n-nahy 'an al-munkar* (enjoining good and forbidding evil), where a pious individual's silent or audible devotion becomes a divine witness against the negligence of their neighbors. It highlights that mere proximity to righteousness is insufficient; one must actively acknowledge and respond to the signs of piety, such as night prayers, to avoid being held accountable on the Day of Judgment.
